info.title: Seattle Solvers Tools API
info.description: FTC parts inventory, search, and receipt reading for tools.seattlesolvers.

post.summary: Create a new team and its first (admin) member
Join an existing team using its invite code
Log in with email and password

get.summary: Get the current user and their team
Get the current team's invite code

patch.description: Requires the current password. Every existing session is revoked, including the token used to make this call — log in again afterwards to get a fresh one.

get.summary: Search the parts library (global + your team's custom parts)
get.description: Anonymous callers see the approved global library. Authenticated callers also see their team's custom parts and an `ownedQuantity` for each result.

post.summary: Add a custom part for your team (optionally submit to the global library)
post.description: Creates a part scoped to your team that you can use immediately. If `submitToLibrary` is true, a copy is queued for Seattle Solvers to review and, if approved, publish to every team.

get.summary: Get a single part by id

patch.summary: Edit one of your team's custom parts
patch.description: Only TEAM-scoped parts your own team created can be edited. Parts in the shared global library are read-only here — submit a correction through an admin instead.

delete.summary: Delete one of your team's custom parts
delete.description: Refused while your team still holds stock of the part — set its inventory quantity to 0 first, so a delete can never silently discard a count.

get.summary: The inventory sheet: parts your team tracks and how many you have

put.summary: Set the quantity (and optional location/notes) of a part

delete.summary: Stop tracking a part (removes the row from your inventory sheet)
delete.description: Different from setting the quantity to 0: that keeps the part on your sheet with no stock, this removes the row entirely. The part itself is untouched.

post.summary: Adjust a part quantity by a delta (e.g. +5 after a purchase, -1 when used)

get.summary: Download the team inventory as CSV

post.summary: Paste an order confirmation (the usual way to add a receipt)
post.description: Send the text of an order confirmation email or web receipt. Plain text and HTML email bodies both work — HTML is detected automatically. Nothing is deciphered here: the characters are already exact, so no OCR and normally no model call is involved. Returns the parsed receipt with matched parts for review; call /confirm to apply it to inventory.

get.summary: List your team's uploaded receipts, newest first

post.summary: Upload a receipt file — a digital PDF invoice, or a photo of a paper receipt
post.description: multipart/form-data with fields `vendor` and `file`. A PDF is read from its text layer, so a downloaded invoice needs no OCR. An image (jpg/png/webp/gif) is OCR'd, falling back to Claude vision only when that is not good enough — this is the physical-receipt path. For an emailed confirmation prefer POST /receipts, which is exact and cheaper.

get.summary: Get a receipt with its parsed line items
Get a short-lived link to a receipt's original file
get.description: The receipts bucket is private, because order confirmations routinely carry a name and shipping address. There is therefore no durable URL to embed: call this when `hasFile` is true and use the returned link, which expires. Returns JSON rather than a redirect so the URL can go straight into an or , which cannot send an Authorization header.

patch.summary: Correct a parsed line item (fix the matched part, quantity, or name)

post.summary: Apply matched line items to your team inventory
post.description: Adds each matched line item's quantity to inventory. Lines without a matched part are skipped and reported. Idempotent per line via the `applied` flag.

get.summary: Get your own team, including its invite code and member count

patch.description: The FTC team number is immutable — it identifies the team and is referenced by submitted parts.

get.summary: List the members of your team

patch.summary: Promote or demote a member of your team
patch.description: Takes effect immediately — the target does not need to log out and back in.

delete.summary: Remove a member from your team
delete.description: Keeps their account but detaches it from the team, so their receipts and submitted parts retain their author. They can join another team (or yours again) with an invite code via POST /teams/join. Access is revoked immediately.

post.summary: Join a team with an invite code, using your existing account
post.description: For accounts that do not currently belong to a team. To sign up and join in one step, use POST /auth/join instead. Leave your current team first if you have one.

post.summary: Issue a new invite code, invalidating the old one
post.description: Use after someone leaves, or if the code was shared more widely than intended.

get.summary: List parts submitted for the global library, pending review

post.summary: Approve a submission — publishes it to the global library for all teams
